title: Episode 3 — Proteus
paragraphs: The inescapable reality of the visible: at least that much, if nothing more, thought through my eyes. Signatures of all things I am here to read — seaweed and wrack, the nearing tide, that rusty boot. Snot-green, blue-silver, rust: colored signs. Limits of the transparent. But Aristotle adds: in bodies. So he was aware of them as bodies before he saw their colors. How? By banging his head against them, of course. Take it easy. Bald he was and a millionaire, the master of those who know. The limit of transparency. Why through? Transparent, opaque. If you can put your five fingers through it, it's a gate; if not, a door. Shut your eyes and see.

Stephen closed his eyes to hear his boots crush crackling wrack and shells. You are walking through it regardless. I am, a stride at a time. A very short space of time through very short times of space. Five, six: one thing after another. Exactly: and that is the inescapable reality of the audible. Open your eyes. No. Jesus! If I fell over a cliff that hangs above the sea, fell through things side by side, inescapably! I am getting on nicely in the dark. My ash-wood sword hangs at my side. Tap with it: that's what blind men do. My two feet in his boots are at the end of his legs, side by side. Sounds solid: made by the hammer of God the Creator. Am I walking into eternity along Sandymount strand? Crush, crack, crick, crick. Wild sea money — shells. Old Deasy the schoolmaster knows all about them.

Won't you come to Sandymount,
Madeline the mare?
Rhythm begins, you see. I hear. A four-beat line of iambs marching. No, galloping: deline the mare.
Open your eyes now. I will. One moment. Has everything vanished since? If I open them and am forever in black darkness. Enough! I will see if I can see.
See now. There all the time without you: and ever shall be, world without end.

They came down the steps from Leahy's terrace cautiously, two women: and down the sloping shore in a clumsy shuffle, their splayed feet sinking in the silted sand. Like me, like Swinburne, coming down to our mighty mother the sea. Number one swung her heavy midwife's bag, the other's umbrella poked in the beach. Out from the Dublin slums for the day. Mrs Florence MacCabe, widow of the late Patrick MacCabe, deeply lamented, of Bride Street. One of her sisterhood hauled me squealing into life. Creation from nothing. What has she in the bag? A stillbirth with a trailing umbilical cord, wrapped in ruddy wool. The cords of all link back, strand-twisting cable of all flesh. That is why mystical monks meditate on the navel. Would you be as gods? Gaze at your navel. Hello. Kinch here. Connect me to the Garden of Eden. Zero, zero, one.

Wife and helpmate of the primal man Adam: Eve, naked Eve. She had no navel. Gaze. Belly without blemish, bulging big, a shield of taut skin, no — white-heaped corn, ageless and immortal, standing from everlasting to everlasting. Womb of sin.

Wombed in sin's darkness I was too, made not begotten. By them, the man with my voice and my eyes and a ghost-woman with ashes on her breath. They embraced and parted, doing the Creator's will. From before the ages He willed me and now may not will me away, ever. An eternal law remains around Him. Is that then the divine substance in which Father and Son are of the same being? Where is poor old Arius to try to settle the question? Fighting his whole life long over the magnificent absurdity of it all. Ill-starred heretic! In a Greek toilet he breathed his last: a good death. Enthroned with beaded bishop's hat and staff, widower of a widowed church, with stiff ceremonial vestment, with clotted backside.
Breezes romped around him, nipping and eager winds. They are coming, waves. The white-maned sea horses, champing, bright-wind-bridled, the steeds of the sea god Mananaan.
I mustn't forget Deasy's letter for the press. And after? The Ship pub, half twelve. By the way, go easy with that money like a good young fool. Yes, I must.

His pace slackened. Here. Am I going to Aunt Sara's or not? My father's voice — my real, flesh-and-blood father's voice. Did you see anything of your artist brother Stephen lately? No? Sure he's not down in Strasburg Terrace with his Aunt Sally? Couldn't he aim a bit higher than that, eh? And and and and tell us, Stephen, how is Uncle Si? Oh, weeping God, the family I married into! The boys up in the hayloft. The drunken little penny-pincher and his brother the cornet player. Very respectable indeed! And cross-eyed Walter calling his father 'sir,' no less! Sir. Yes, sir. No, sir. Jesus wept: and no wonder, by Christ!
I pull the wheezy bell of their shuttered cottage: and wait. They take me for a bill collector, peer out from a hidden vantage point.
—It's Stephen, sir.
—Let him in. Let Stephen in.
A bolt drawn back and Walter welcomes me.
—We thought you were someone else.
In his broad bed Uncle Richie, propped up on pillows and blanketed, extends over the hillock of his knees a sturdy forearm. Clean-chested. He has washed the upper half.
—Good morning, nephew.

He sets aside the writing board on which he drafts his legal bills for his employers Goff and Shapland Tandy, filing consent forms and common searches and a court summons. A dark oak frame over his bald head: Oscar Wilde's poem Requiescat. The drone of his tuneless whistle brings Walter back.
—Yes, sir?
—Whiskey for Richie and Stephen, tell mother. Where is she?
—Bathing Crissie, sir.
Papa's little bed companion. Darling child.
—No, Uncle Richie...
—Call me Richie. Damn your mineral water. It's depressing. Whiskey!
—Uncle Richie, really...
—Sit down or I swear I'll knock you down.
Walter squints vainly for a chair.
—He has nothing to sit down on, sir.

—He has nowhere to put it, you idiot. Bring in our fancy chair. Would you like a bite of something? None of your fancy airs here. How about a nice rasher fried with a herring? Sure? So much the better. We have nothing in the house but aspirin.
Attention!
He hums bars of Fernando's entrance aria from the opera. The grandest number, Stephen, in the whole opera. Listen.
His tuneful whistle sounds again, finely shaded, with rushes of melody, his fists drumming on his padded knees.
This breeze is sweeter.

Houses of decay, mine, his and all. You told the boys at Clongowes school you had an uncle who was a judge and an uncle who was a general in the army. Leave them behind, Stephen. Beauty is not there. Nor in the stagnant bay of Marsh's library where you read the fading prophecies of Joachim of Fiore. For whom? The vulgar mob of the cathedral close. A hater of his kind ran from them to the madwood, his mane foaming in the moon, his eyeballs stars. Horse-nostrilled. The long oval faces: Temple, Buck Mulligan, Foxy Campbell, Lantern-jaws. Abbot father, furious dean, what offense set fire to their brains? Pah! Come down, bald man, before you go completely bald. A garland of grey hair on his condemned head, see him — me — clambering down to the altar step (Come down!), clutching a sacred vessel, with a basilisk's eyes. Get down, baldy! A choir gives back menace and echo, gathered around the altar, the snorted Latin of jackpriests moving heavily in their white robes, tonsured and oiled and castrated, fat with the fat of kidneys of wheat.

And at the same instant perhaps a priest around the corner is elevating the host. Ding-ding! And two streets away another locking it into a sacred box. Ding-a-ding! And in a lady chapel another eating the body of Christ all to himself. Ding-ding! Down, up, forward, back. William of Ockham thought of that, the invincible logician. A misty English morning, the imp of philosophical puzzles tickled his brain. Bringing down the host and kneeling, he heard twining with his second bell the first bell in the transept (he is lifting his) and, rising, heard (now I am lifting mine) their two bells (he is kneeling) chime together in harmony.

Cousin Stephen, you will never be a saint. Island of saints, they call Ireland. You were awfully holy, weren't you? You prayed to the Blessed Virgin that you might not have a red nose. You prayed to the devil on Serpentine Avenue that the chubby widow ahead might lift her skirts still higher from the wet street. Oh yes, certainly! Sell your soul for that, do — dyed rags pinned around a frumpy woman. Tell me more, more still! On top of the Howth tram, alone, crying to the rain: Naked women! Naked women! What about that, eh?
What about what? What else were they invented for?

Reading two pages each of seven books every night, eh? I was young. You bowed to yourself in the mirror, stepping forward to imaginary applause, striking a pose. Hurray for the goddamn idiot! Hurray! No one saw: tell no one. Books you were going to write with single letters for titles. Have you read his F? Oh yes, but I prefer Q. Yes, but W is wonderful. Oh yes, W. Remember your little revelations written on green oval leaves, deep beyond deep, copies to be sent if you died to all the great libraries of the world, including Alexandria? Someone was to read them there after a few thousand years, a cosmic age from now. Like Pico della Mirandola. Yes, very like a whale. When one reads these strange pages of one long gone one feels that one is at one with one who once...

The grainy sand had gone from under his feet. His boots trod again a damp crackling mass of seaweed, razor shells, squeaking pebbles that beat upon the unnumbered stones, wood eaten by shipworms, lost Armada. Unwholesome sand flats waited to suck at his soles, breathing upward sewage breath. A pocket of seaweed smoldered in phosphorescent fire under a heap of human refuse. He skirted them, walking warily. A porter bottle stood up, stuck to its waist in the cakey sand dough. A sentinel: isle of dreadful thirst. Broken barrel hoops on the shore; inland a maze of dark cunning fishing nets; farther away chalk-scrawled back doors and on the higher beach a clothesline with two crucified shirts. Ringsend: shanties of brown-skinned seamen and ship captains. Human shells.
He halted. I have passed the turn to Aunt Sara's. Am I not going there? Seems not. No one about. He turned northeast and crossed the firmer sand toward the Pigeonhouse power station.
—Who got you into this awful mess?
—It was the pigeon — the Holy Spirit — Joseph.

Patrice, home on leave, drank warm milk with me in the bar MacMahon in Paris. Son of the wild goose — an Irish exile — Kevin Egan of Paris. My father's a bird, he lapped the sweet warm milk with pink young tongue, plump bunny's face. Lap, little rabbit. He hopes to win the lottery. He read Michelet on the nature of women. But he must send me The Life of Jesus by that hoaxer Léo Taxil. Lent it to his friend.
—It's hilarious, you know. Me, I'm a socialist. I don't believe in the existence of God. But don't tell my father.
—He believes?
—My father, yes.
End of conversation. He drinks his milk.

My Latin Quarter hat. God, we simply must dress the part. I want purple gloves. You were a student, weren't you? Of what, for the love of God? Science. P.C.N., you know: physics, chemistry, and natural sciences. Ah. Eating your cheap stew, flesh-pots of Egypt, elbowed by belching cab drivers. Just say in the most natural tone: when I was in Paris, on the Boulevard Saint-Michel, I used to. Yes, used to carry punched tickets to prove an alibi if they arrested you for murder somewhere. Justice. On the night of the seventeenth of February 1904 the prisoner was seen by two witnesses. Some other fellow did it: some other me. Hat, tie, overcoat, nose. Him — that's me. You seem to have enjoyed yourself.

Proudly walking. Who were you trying to walk like? Never mind: a dispossessed man. With mother's money order, eight shillings, the banging door of the post office slammed in your face by the clerk. Hunger and toothache. Two more minutes. Check the clock. Must hurry. Closed. Hired thug! Shoot him to bloody bits with a shotgun, bits of man splattered on walls, all brass buttons. Bits all clicking back into place. Not hurt? Oh, that's all right. Shake hands. See what I meant? Oh, that's all right. Shake hands. Oh, that's all just fine.

You were going to do wonders, weren't you? Missionary to Europe after the fiery Saint Columban. The Irish monks Fiacre and Scotus on their heavenly thrones, laughing out of their pint glasses, loud Latin laughter: Bravo! Bravo! Pretending to speak broken English as you dragged your suitcase, tipping the porter threepence, across the slimy pier at Newhaven. What? Rich booty you brought back: a naughty French magazine, five tattered issues of a comic paper, a blue French telegram, a curiosity to show:
—Mother dying come home father.
The aunt thinks you killed your mother. That's why she won't.

Then here's a health to Mulligan's aunt
And I'll tell you the reason why.
She always kept things decent in
The Hannigan family.

His feet marched in sudden proud rhythm over the sand furrows, along by the boulders of the south wall. He stared at them proudly, piled stone mammoth skulls. Gold light on sea, on sand, on boulders. The sun is there, the slender trees, the lemon-colored houses.

Paris waking raw, crude sunlight on her lemon streets. Moist insides of bread rolls, the frog-green wormwood liquor — absinthe — her morning incense, flavoring the air. A handsome man rises from the bed of his wife's lover's wife. The kerchiefed housewife is astir, a saucer of vinegar in her hand. In Rodot's café Yvonne and Madeleine fix their tumbled beauty, crunching with gold teeth pastries, their mouths yellowed with custard. Faces of Parisian men go by, pleased with their pleasures, curled like conquistadors.

Noon slumbers. Kevin Egan rolls gunpowder cigarettes through fingers smeared with printer's ink, sipping his green absinthe as his son Patrice sips his white wine. Around us diners fork spiced beans down their throats. A half-pint, please! A jet of coffee steam from the burnished urn. She serves me at his signal. He's Irish. Dutch? No, not cheese. Two Irishmen, we are, from Ireland, you know, ah yes! She thought you wanted Dutch cheese. Your post-prandial drink — do you know that word? Post-prandial. There was a fellow I knew once in Barcelona, odd fellow, used to call it his post-prandial. Well: cheers! Around the slabbed tables the tangle of wine-soaked breaths and rumbling stomachs. His breath hangs over our sauce-stained plates, the green fairy's fang of absinthe thrusting between his lips. Of Ireland, the warriors of Brian Boru, of hopes, conspiracies, of Arthur Griffith the nationalist, the mystical poet A.E., good shepherd of men. Trying to yoke me as his fellow revolutionary, our crimes our common cause. You're your father's son. I know the voice. His worn shirt, decorated with red flowers, trembles its Spanish tassels at his secrets. Drumont, famous French journalist — know what he called Queen Victoria? Old hag with the yellow teeth. Old ogress with the yellow teeth. Maud Gonne, beautiful woman, for the Fatherland. Millevoye, Félix Faure — know how Faure died? Lustful men. The Scandinavian girl, maid of all work, who rubs men naked in the bath at Uppsala. It's my job, she said, all the gentlemen. Not this gentleman, I said. Most indecent custom. A bath is a most private thing. I wouldn't let my brother, not even my own brother, it's most indecent. Green eyes, I see you. Fangs, I feel. Lustful people.

The blue fuse of his cigarette burns deadly between hands and burns clear. Loose tobacco shreds catch fire: a flame and acrid smoke light our corner. Raw cheekbones under his rebel's cap. How the rebel leader escaped, the real story. Disguised as a young bride, man in veil and orange blossoms, drove out the road to Malahide. He did, truly. Tales of lost leaders, the betrayed, wild escapes. Disguises snatched at, gone, not here.

Spurned lover. I was a strapping young lad at that time, I tell you. I'll show you my picture one day. I was, truly. A lover — for her love, for Ireland's love, he prowled with Colonel Richard Burke, chieftain of his clan, under the walls of Clerkenwell Prison and, crouching, saw a flame of vengeance hurl them upward in the fog. Shattered glass and toppling masonry. In gay Paris he hides, Egan of Paris, sought by no one save by me. Making his daily rounds: the dingy print shop, his three taverns, the Montmartre den where he sleeps short nights, in the street of the Golden Drop, decorated with flyblown photographs of the dead. Loveless, landless, wifeless. She is quite comfortably settled without her outcast man, the madam on the Street of the Lying Heart, with a canary and two male lodgers. Peachy cheeks, a striped skirt, frisky as a young thing. Spurned and undespairing. Tell Pat you saw me, won't you? I wanted to get poor Pat a job one time. My son, soldier of France. I taught him to sing The Boys of Kilkenny Are Stout Roaring Blades. Know that old tune? I taught Patrice that. Old Kilkenny: Saint Canice's city, Strongbow's castle on the River Nore. Goes like this. Oh, oh. He takes my hand, like Napper Tandy in the song.

Oh, oh the boys of
Kilkenny...
Weak wasting hand on mine. They have forgotten Kevin Egan, not he them. Remembering thee, O Zion.

He had come nearer the edge of the sea and wet sand slapped his boots. The new air greeted him, harping on wild nerves, wind of wild air carrying seeds of brightness. Wait — I'm not walking out to the Kish lighthouse, am I? He stopped suddenly, his feet beginning to sink slowly in the quaking soil. Turn back.

Turning, he scanned the shore southward, his feet sinking again slowly in new depressions. The cold domed room of the tower waits. Through the narrow windows the shafts of light move ever onward, slowly ever as my feet are sinking, creeping duskward across the floor. Blue dusk, nightfall, deep blue night. In the darkness of the dome they wait, their pushed-back chairs, my battered suitcase, around a table of abandoned plates. Who will clear them? He has the key. I will not sleep there when night comes. A shut door of a silent tower, entombing their blind bodies, the panther-dreaming Englishman and his gun dog. Call: no answer. He lifted his feet from the sucking sand and turned back by the wall of boulders. Take everything, keep everything. My soul walks with me, the form of forms. So in the moon's midnight watches I pace the path above the rocks, in dark silver, hearing Elsinore's tempting flood.

The flood is following me. I can watch it flow past from here. Better get back by the Poolbeg road to the strand. He climbed over the sedge and eel-like seaweed and sat on a stool of rock, resting his walking stick in a crevice.

A bloated carcass of a dog lay sprawled on bladder-wrack seaweed. Before him the side of a boat, sunk in sand. A coach stuck in sand — that's what the French critic Louis Veuillot called Théophile Gautier's prose. These heavy sands are language, tide and wind have silted here. And these, the stone heaps of dead builders, a warren of rat warrens. Hide gold there. Try it. You have some. Sands and stones. Weight of the past. Some giant's toys. Mind you don't get one good smack on the ear. I'm the bloody great giant who rolls all these bloody great boulders, bones for my stepping stones. Fee-fi-fo-fum. I smell the blood of an Irishman.

A point, a live dog, grew into sight running across the sweep of sand. Lord, is he going to attack me? Respect his freedom. You will not be master of others or their slave. I have my stick. Sit tight. From farther away, walking shoreward from the crested tide, figures, two. The two Marys — like those at Christ's tomb. They have tucked it safe among the bulrushes. Peekaboo. I see you. No, the dog. He is running back to them. Who?

Galleys of the Vikings ran here to beach, in quest of prey, their blood-beaked prows riding low on a molten pewter surf. Danish Vikings, gold neck-rings and hatchets aglitter on their chests, when the Irish king Malachi wore the collar of gold. A school of whales stranded in hot noon, spouting, floundering in the shallows. Then from the starving walled city a horde of ragged dwarfs, my people, with butchers' knives, running, climbing, hacking in green blubbery whale meat. Famine, plague and slaughters. Their blood is in me, their passions my waves. I moved among them on the frozen River Liffey, I, a changeling, among the sputtering bonfires. I spoke to no one: none to me.

The dog's bark ran toward him, stopped, ran back. Dog of my enemy. I just stood there pale, silent, surrounded by barking. Meditating terrible things. A man in a primrose-colored jacket, fortune's favorite, smiled at my fear. Is that what you pine for — the bark of their applause? Pretenders: living their lives. The Bruce's brother, Thomas Fitzgerald the silken knight, Perkin Warbeck, York's false heir in breeches of white-rose ivory, wonder of a day, and Lambert Simnel with a train of nuns and camp followers, a kitchen boy crowned king. All kings' sons. Paradise of pretenders then and now. He saved men from drowning and you tremble at a dog's yelping. But the courtiers who mocked the poet Guido in his own city's church were on their own turf. House of... We don't want any of your medieval obscurities. Would you do what he did? A boat would be near, a life buoy. Naturally — put there for you. Would you or wouldn't you? The man who drowned nine days ago off Maiden's Rock. They are waiting for him now. The truth, spit it out. I would want to. I would try. I am not a strong swimmer. Water cold soft. When I put my face into it in the basin at Clongowes school. Can't see! Who's behind me? Out quickly, quickly! Do you see the tide flowing quickly in on all sides, sheeting the low sandbars quickly, shell-cocoa-colored? If I had solid ground under my feet. I want his life still to be his, mine to be mine. A drowning man. His human eyes scream to me out of the horror of his death. I... Together with him, down... I could not save her. Waters: bitter death: lost.
A woman and a man. I see her skirts. Pinned up, I bet.

Their dog ambled about a bank of thinning sand, trotting, sniffing on all sides. Looking for something lost in a past life. Suddenly he bolted like a hare, ears flung back, chasing the shadow of a low-skimming gull. The man's shrieked whistle struck his limp ears. He turned, bounded back, came nearer, trotted on twinkling legs. Like a heraldic deer on a tawny field, bounding, noble, free. At the lace-edge of the tide he halted with stiff forelegs, ears pointed seaward. His snout lifted, barking at the wave noise, herds of sea horses. They serpented toward his feet, curling, unfurling many crests, every ninth one breaking, splashing, from far, from farther out, waves and waves.

Cockle pickers. They waded a little way into the water and, stooping, dunked their bags and, lifting them again, waded out. The dog yelped, running to them, reared up and pawed them, dropping on all fours, rearing up again at them with mute bearish affection. Unheeded, he kept by them as they came toward drier sand, a rag of wolf's tongue red-panting from his jaws. His speckled body ambled ahead of them and then loped off at a calf's gallop. The carcass lay on his path. He stopped, sniffed, stalked round it, brother, nosing closer, went round it, sniffing rapidly like a dog all over the dead dog's bedraggled coat. Dog skull, dog sniff, eyes on the ground, moves toward one great goal. Ah, poor dogsbody! Here lies poor dogsbody's body.
—Tatters! Get away from that, you mongrel!

The cry brought him skulking back to his master and a blunt bootless kick sent him unharmed across a spit of sand, crouched in flight. He slunk back in a curve. He doesn't see me. Along the edge of the stone wall he lolloped, dawdled, smelled a rock and from under a cocked hind leg pissed against it. He trotted forward and, lifting his hind leg again, pissed quick and short at a rock he hadn't sniffed. The simple pleasures of the poor. His back paws then scattered the sand: then his front paws dabbled and delved. Something he buried there, his grandmother. He rooted in the sand, dabbling, delving, and stopped to listen to the air, scraped up the sand again with a fury of his claws, soon ceasing, a leopard, a panther, born of an illicit union, preying on the dead.

After he woke me last night — the same dream or was it? Wait. Open hallway. Street of prostitutes. Remember. Haroun al Rashid from the Arabian Nights. I'm almost getting it. That man led me, spoke. I was not afraid. The melon he held against my face. Smiled: sweet cream-fruit smell. That was the rule, he said. In. Come. Red carpet spread. You will see who.

Shouldering their bags they trudged, the dark-skinned wanderers. His blue-cold feet out of turned-up trousers slapped the clammy sand, a dull brick scarf strangling his unshaven neck. With a woman's steps she followed: the rogue and his wandering woman. Her pickings slung at her back. Loose sand and crushed shells caked on her bare feet. About her wind-raw face hair trailed. Behind her lord, his helpmate, tramping off to nowhere. When night hides her body's flaws she calls from an archway where dogs have fouled. Her fancy man is buying drinks for two Royal Dublin Fusiliers in O'Loughlin's pub in Blackpitts. Kiss her, trade slang with her in rogues' street talk, for oh, my sweet wanton darling! A she-devil's whiteness under her rank rags. Fumbally's lane that night: the smell of the tannery.

White your hands, red your mouth
And your body's soft and fine.
Let me lie with you then.
In the darkness hold and kiss.

Gloomy pleasure, as the pot-bellied monk Aquinas calls it, you old porcupine friar. Adam before the Fall made love and did not merely rut. Call away, let him say: your body's soft and fine. Language no worse than his own. Monks' words, rosary beads jangling at their belts: rogues' words, hard coins rattling in their pockets.
Passing now.

A sideways glance at my Hamlet hat. If I were suddenly naked here as I sit? I am not. Across the sands of all the world, followed by the sun's flaming sword, to the west, trekking to evening lands. She trudges, hauls, drags, pulls her load. A tide westering, moon-drawn, in her wake. Tides, with their myriad islands, within her, blood not mine, upon the wine-dark sea. Behold the handmaid of the moon. In sleep the wet sign calls her hour, bids her rise. Bridal bed, childbed, bed of death, ghost-candled. All flesh shall come to you. He comes, pale vampire, through storm his eyes, his bat sails bloodying the sea, mouth to her mouth's kiss.
Here. Put a pin in that thought, will you? My notebook. Mouth to her kiss. No. Must be two of them. Stick them together. Mouth to her mouth's kiss.

His lips shaped and mouthed fleshless lips of air: mouth to her womb. Womb, all-wombing tomb. His mouth molded outgoing breath, unspoken: ooeeehah: roar of planets plunging catastrophically, globed, blazing, roaring wayawayawayawayaway. Paper. The banknotes, damn them. Old Deasy's letter. Here. Thanking you for the hospitality — tear the blank end off. Turning his back to the sun he bent far over a table of rock and scribbled words. That's twice I forgot to take blank slips from the library counter.

His shadow lay over the rocks as he bent, ending. Why not endless to the farthest star? Darkly they are there behind this light, darkness shining in the brightness, the constellation Cassiopeia, other worlds. Here I sit with my diviner's rod of ash wood, in borrowed sandals, by day beside a dull sea, unseen, in violet night walking beneath a sky of strange stars. I throw this finished shadow from me, the inescapable human shape, call it back. Endless, would it be mine, form of my form? Who watches me here? Who anywhere will ever read these written words? Signs on a white field. Somewhere to someone in your most lyrical voice. The philosopher Bishop Berkeley took the veil of appearances out of his top hat: the veil of space with colored patterns woven on it. Hold on. Colors on a flat surface: yes, that's right. Flat I see, then think distance, near, far, flat I see, east, back. Ah, see now! It falls back suddenly, frozen in three dimensions. Click does the trick. You find my words dark. Darkness is in our souls, don't you think? More lyrically. Our souls, shame-wounded by our sins, cling to us yet more, as a woman to her lover clinging, the more the more.

She trusts me, her hand gentle, the long-lashed eyes. Now where the blue hell am I leading her beyond the veil of appearances? Into the inescapable reality of the inescapable visible. She, she, she. What she? The young woman at the bookshop window on Monday looking in for one of the alphabet-titled books you were going to write. The keen glance you gave her. Her wrist through the braided loop of her parasol handle. She lives in Leeson Park with a companion and dainty dishes, a literary lady. Tell that to someone else, Stevie: pick me up at a party. Bet she wears those God-awful corsets and yellow stockings, darned with lumpy wool. Talk about dumpy women — forget about it. Where are your wits?
Touch me. Soft eyes. Soft soft soft hand. I am lonely here. Oh, touch me soon, now. What is that word known to all men? I am quiet here alone. Sad too. Touch, touch me.

He lay back at full stretch over the sharp rocks, cramming the scribbled note and pencil into a pocket, his hat tilted down over his eyes. That is Kevin Egan's gesture I just made, nodding for his nap, his sabbath sleep. And God saw. And it was very good. Hey! Good morning. Welcome as the flowers in May. Under its leaf he watched through peacock-twittering lashes the southward-moving sun. I am caught in this burning scene. Pan's hour, the faun's noon. Among gum-heavy serpent-plants, milk-oozing fruits, where on the tawny waters leaves lie wide. Pain is far.
And no more turn aside and brood.

His gaze brooded on his broad-toed boots, a rich man's cast-offs, side by side. He counted the creases of rucked leather where another's foot had nested warm. The foot that beat the ground in dance, the foot I dislike. But you were delighted when Esther Osvalt's shoe fit you: girl I knew in Paris. Oh, what a pretty little foot! A true friend, a soul brother: Wilde's love that dare not speak its name. His arm: Cranly's arm. He will leave me now. And the blame? I am as I am. All or not at all.

In long loops from the Cock lake the water flowed full, covering in green-gold the lagoons of sand, rising, flowing. My walking stick will float away. I shall wait. No, they will pass on, passing, rubbing against the low rocks, swirling, passing. Better get this business over quickly. Listen: a four-worded wave-speech: seesoo, hrss, rsseeiss, ooos. Powerful breath of waters amid sea-snakes, rearing horses, rocks. In cups of rocks it slops: flop, slop, slap: bounded in barrels. And spent, its speech ceases. It flows purling, widely flowing, floating foam-pool, flower unfurling.

Under the up-swelling tide he saw the writhing weeds lift languidly and sway reluctant arms, lifting their petticoats in whispering water, swaying and upturning shy silver fronds. Day by day: night by night: lifted, flooded and let fall. Lord, they are weary; and, whispered to, they sigh. Saint Ambrose heard it, the sigh of leaves and waves, waiting, awaiting the fullness of their times, suffering injuries day and night and groaning. Gathered to no end; vainly then released, flowing forth, winding back: drawn by the moon. Weary too in the sight of lovers, lustful men; a naked woman gleaming in her chambers, she draws a net of waters.

Five fathoms out there. Full fathom five thy father lies. At one o'clock, they said. Found drowned. High water at Dublin bar. Driving before it a loose drift of rubble, drifting schools of fish, silly shells. A corpse rising salt-white from the undertow, bobbing a pace a pace a porpoise landward. There he is. Hook it quick. Pull. Sunk though he be beneath the watery floor. We have him. Easy now.

Bag of corpse-gas sopping in foul brine. A quiver of minnows, fat of a spongy morsel, flash through the slits of his buttoned trouser fly. God becomes man becomes fish becomes barnacle goose becomes featherbed mountain. Dead men's breaths I, living, breathe; I tread dead dust, devour foul remains from all the dead. Hauled stiff over the side of a boat he breathes upward the stench of his green grave, his rotting nostrils snoring to the sun.

A sea-change this, brown eyes turned salt-blue. Sea-death, mildest of all deaths known to man. Old Father Ocean. Prize of Paris: beware of imitations. Just give it a fair trial. We enjoyed ourselves immensely.

Come. I'm thirsty. Clouding over. No black clouds anywhere though, are there? Thunderstorm. All-bright he falls, proud lightning of the intellect, Lucifer, I say, who knows no setting. No. My pilgrim's hat and staff and my sandal shoes. Where? To evening lands. Evening will find itself.

He took the handle of his walking stick, lunging with it softly, dallying still. Yes, evening will find itself in me, without me. All days make their end. By the way, next — when is it? Tuesday will be the longest day. Of all the glad new year, mother, the rum tum tiddledy tum. Tennyson, gentleman poet. Indeed. For the old hag with the yellow teeth — that's what they called Queen Victoria. And Monsieur Drumont, gentleman journalist. Indeed. My teeth are very bad. Why, I wonder. Feel. That one is going too. Shells — teeth like shells. Ought I go to a dentist, I wonder, with that money? That one. This one. Toothless Kinch, the superman. Why is that, I wonder, or does it mean something perhaps?
My handkerchief. He threw it. I remember. Did I not pick it up?
His hand groped vainly in his pockets. No, I didn't. Better buy one.
He placed the dry snot picked from his nostril on a ledge of rock, carefully. As for the rest, let whoever wants to look.
Behind me. Perhaps there is someone.

He turned his face over his shoulder, looking back. Moving through the air, the tall masts of a three-masted ship, her sails furled up on the yards, homeward bound, upstream, silently moving, a silent ship.
